reason: Attacked and not broken, but the Penguin page is still unseen, so this stays a hedge. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Mencius 1 of 3 in the year (month 2, the Book II Part A 6 line, same source format), not banned, and no second Mencius elsewhere in month 4. In scope (a named work, philosophy, not the scripture the brief excludes), publishable, on theme, tag Philosophy is the form, source leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote, 61 characters. What I could not do: reach D. C. Lau. The Internet Archive holds the 1970 Penguin (mencius00menc) and two later printings, all lending-restricted, and search inside returns Item not available without a borrower session; Google Books was unreachable too. Every open search returns Legge (The way of truth is like a great road. It is not difficult to know it. The evil is only that men will not seek it), a different translation and NOT what the card prints, so at least there is no drift into Legge. The single witness to Lau remains the file770 essay, and I tested it rather than trusting it: it quotes four Lau passages with bracketed locators and page numbers, and those pages are internally coherent once its typo is seen (its IV:A:15 is the famous VI:A:15 organs of sight and hearing passage, p. 168; VI:A:18 p. 169; VI:B:2 p. 172; VII:A:37 p. 190, a rising sequence that fits one continuous Penguin text). That is a transcription with locators, not a quotation-site paraphrase, and it agrees word for word with the three sentences the card prints. NOT REFUTED, but two defects to fix before landing. First, the note is wrong in the one place it speaks confidently: it says the closing sentence about going home and finding teachers enough could not be found in Lau and may be a reconstruction. That sentence is certainly in Mencius VI.B.2 (Legge: Do you go home and search for it, and you will have abundance of teachers), so the note as written invites a reader to think the passage ends at the third sentence or that the fourth is invented. Ending the card at the third sentence is fine; what the note should say is that the card stops early and that the printed page was not opened, not that the sentence may be a reconstruction. Second, the hedge is missing from the note entirely: the evidence field admits the Penguin page was not seen, the note does not, and rule 12 wants that said plainly on the card. betterCitation adds the page the one witness attests, so a reader can check it in a single move.
betterCitation: Mencius, Mencius, Book VI, Part B, 2, p. 172 (trans. D. C. Lau, 1970)
